text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired -> PD#INC-4521 - high 5xx rate on /v1/generate (service: redwood-runtime). link: https://pd.example/INC-4521

pagerduty-bot: Escalation policy: oncall-runtime -> paging in 30s if unacked. Incident details: approx 3k errors/min from eu-west-1, error fingerprint = upstream-connection-reset.

alice (oncall): acked. I'm looking. Thanks for the ping.

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by alice (oncall) at 2026-03-14T10:06:40Z.

alice (oncall): quick checks: dashboards show 5xx spike started ~10:05 UTC, errors across 6 hosts, p50 latency up 30ms only. Customer impact: a portion of streaming responses failing. Not universal but several PLG customers reporting partial failures.

ben (infra): logs show upstream pool returning ECONNRESET from model-proxy. snippet: ```2026-03-14T10:05:12Z ERROR model-proxy: connection reset by peer, retrying (host=ip-10-0-5-12)``` Looks like a networking transient or model backend OOM. Spreading across hosts suggests a shared dependency.

charlie SRE: could be a routing change or LB health checks flapping. We should avoid immediate full-team paging if PD is duping for each host. Can we silence duplicates and keep one alert?

alice (oncall): agree. This looks like a paging storm: multiple similar alerts firing for the same logical failure. I'll create a temporary silence for PD alerts for redwood-runtime and open a short suppression in incident-bot to avoid re-paging while we remediate.

ben (infra): running silence now: ```pctl silence create --service=redwood-runtime --duration=20m --reason="paging storm - grouping duplicates" --scope=eu-west-1```

ben (infra): output: ```Silence created: S-789e, expires 2026-03-14T10:26:40Z. PagerDuty notifications suppressed for matching alerts.``` :white_check_mark:

incidents-bot: Temporary suppression applied to alerts matching fingerprint upstream-connection-reset in eu-west-1 for 20m. Auto-grouping threshold=3 hosts.

alice (oncall): I'm going to open a read-only maintenance window in the incident-bot to avoid noisy re-fires while we triage. Also starting a canary scale to shift some traffic to fallback-model.

dana (support): heard from one enterprise customer (Acct: ACME) saying their requests timed out ~10:06-10:10. They've got an SLO but haven't opened a ticket yet. Flagging for postmortem.

charlie SRE: mitigation checklist: 1) enable fallback routing 2) scale model-proxy pool + health-check stabilization 3) patch LB idle timeouts 4) observe for 5m. I'll run the playbook for connection-reset storms.

ben (infra): executing quickscale: ```kubectl -n runtime scale deployment/model-proxy --replicas=12```

ben (infra): quick health restart on the 3 flapping pods: ```kubectl -n runtime rollout restart deployment/model-proxy --selector=host=eu-west-1-flap```. Logs show restart started.

alice (oncall): toggled fallback routing to fallback-model-v2 for 25% traffic. Command: ```rctl route set /v1/generate fallback=fallback-model-v2 --percent=25```. Monitoring.

incidents-bot: alert dedupe: currently grouping by alert name + fingerprint; suggestion: switch to fingerprint-only grouping for this class to prevent host-level noise. Created temp config change: ```group_by: [fingerprint] auto_group_window: 120s max_group_size: 25```

alice (oncall): after scale + restarts, error rate dropped from 3k/min to ~120/min in 5m. p50 latency returning to normal. Watch for re-surge.

pagerduty-bot: If incident is stable for 15m, will auto-resolve. Next escalation in policy if re-fired.

dana (support): ACME confirmed degraded experience but not total outage. Opening a support ticket and sending status update.

charlie SRE: note for follow-up: incident-bot housekeeping needed — create a permanent suppression rule for upstream-connection-reset storms: require grouping by fingerprint across hosts, and a cooldown window of 3m before additional pages. Also add auto-silence on >500 alerts/min from same fingerprint for 15m. I'll open a ticket.

alice (oncall): handoff: I'm on for another 8 minutes, then handing to ben for the 10:30 shift. Ben, please take over if it reappears.

ben (infra): ack. I'll monitor metrics and keep silence if duplicates continue. Created Jira: RINF-2317 "Adjust incident-bot grouping and add paging storm safeguards" assigned to charlie.

incidents-bot: Incident INC-4521 status: stable, notifications suppressed. Will auto-resolve at 2026-03-14T10:26:40Z if no new alerts.

alice (oncall): thanks everyone. Add to postmortem: root cause unknown (likely upstream model-proxy transient or network), remed steps (scale, restart, fallback), and action items (grouping tweak, auto-silence rules, runbook update, ACME follow-up). :memo:

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-4521 resolved by system at 2026-03-14T10:26:41Z. Resolution note: error rate returned to baseline after autoscale + restarts.

incidents-bot: housekeeping: deleting old silences older than 72h flagged. Reminder: runbook update PR requested in #eng-sre.

charlie SRE: reopening ticket for longer-term fix: investigate model-proxy connection handling under burst and health-check tuning. Will add simulation tests.

alice (oncall): handing off: ben gets primary, charlie gets secondary. I'll post final summary in incidents channel and mark PD incident closed. Good job everyone :tada:

ben (infra): final check: metrics link https://metrics.example/graph?insight=errors&inc=INC-4521. No new alerts in 12m. Closing monitoring loop. :white_check_mark:
